personality_one_liner: A trustworthy, clean, and structured environment that balances high-density property management data with an inviting, imagery-rich public marketplace.

spacing.rule: Generous padding around content. Clear grouping of elements. Do not leave accidental empty space on the right side of cards. Sticky primary CTAs over scrolling content.

do's: Bottom tab bar when content scrolls behind it
Featured/hero cards frosted glass overlay on brand-tinted or photo backdrop
Sticky horizontal chip bar for filters on the search screen
dont's: Every button, list rows, chips, cards in dense lists, form inputs
Foreground readability failure (use underlying tint opacity >=70% if needed)

screens.name: Public Visitor - Search & Explore
screens.purpose: Allow users to search, filter, and discover hostels/PGs with high-quality imagery and clear pricing.

states.loading: Skeleton loading cards with image placeholders
states.empty: Illustration of a house with 'No hostels found in this area. Try adjusting your filters.' + 'Reset Filters' CTA

screens.layout: Row 1: Sticky search field and sort/filter buttons. Row 2: Sticky horizontal scrollable filter chips (Boys/Girls, AC/Non-AC, Price). Below: Full-width list of hostel cards. Each card has a large hero image, a gradient scrim at the bottom with the Hostel Name, rating, and price. Verified badge floating at the top right.

screens.name: Hostel Owner - Dashboard
screens.purpose: Provide property owners a quick glance at their occupancy, pending collections, and daily operations.

states.empty: 'Add your first hostel/building to start managing' + 'Add Property' Primary CTA
states.error: 'Could not load dashboard data' + Retry button

screens.layout: Progressive disclosure structure. Top section: Horizontal scroll of primary KPI stat cards (Occupancy %, Monthly Collection, Pending Rent). Below: Quick Actions grid (2-col grid for Add Tenant, Add Room, Collect Rent). Bottom: List of 'Today's Check-ins/Outs' and recent complaints.

screens.name: Admin - Platform Dashboard
screens.purpose: Platform owner overview of total properties, revenue, and pending approvals.

states.error: 'Failed to load admin stats' + Retry button

screens.layout: Data-dense but clean single-column flow. Top KPI cards (Total Hostels, Premium Plans Active). Next section: 'Pending Verifications' list where each list item has 'Approve' and 'Reject' quick-action buttons directly on the row to save taps.

screens.name: Tenant - My Room & Rent
screens.purpose: Tenant self-service portal to view room details, pay rent, and track history.

states.error: 'Could not load tenant details' + Retry button

screens.layout: Profile cover banner at top. Large 'Rent Status' card prominently displayed (Due / Paid) with a sticky primary 'Pay Rent' CTA at the bottom if due. Below rent card: Room details (Floor, Bed No, WiFi password) and 'Recent Receipts' list.

instructions_to_main_agent: Strictly follow the No-Tolerance rule for colors: DO NOT use any shade of Blue, Navy, Purple, or Indigo. The primary brand color is Deep Emerald/Moss Green (#2C5E3E) which signals stability and shelter without falling into the generic AI-blue trap.

The app has 4 distinct roles. Implement Role-Based Access Control logic for the default landing screens. Admin sees System Dashboard, Owner sees Property Dashboard, Tenant sees My Room, Visitor sees Public Search.
Implement the 'Sticky primary CTA' pattern for major forms (Add Tenant, Pay Rent) so it floats above the scrollable content.
For the Public Search screen, implement a sticky horizontal scrollable filter chip bar. This allows quick filtering without navigating away from the list.
Ensure every property list card features a real image from the image slots and has a bottom gradient scrim (transparent to surfaceInverse) so text overlaid on it is readable.
Admin verification rows should surface 'Approve'/'Reject' actions directly on the list item to avoid unnecessary drill-down navigation.
When displaying stats in Owner/Admin dashboards, use progressive disclosure. Put the most important KPIs (Occupancy, Revenue) in large cards, and secondary details in smaller lists below.
